sentences.text:
This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed Challenging the award passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Court II), Small Causes, Chennai, made in M.C.O.P.No.1430 of 2016 dated 05.09.2024.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Court II), Small Causes, Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company has raised the following grounds:-

(I) I submit that the Hon'ble Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact that it was the rider of the motorcycle who dashed behind the II Respondent's lorry, resulting in the alleged road traffic accident.

(ii) I Submit that the Hon'ble Tribunal failed to consider the fact that the alleged accident had occurred in broad day light and that the deceased rider of the motorcycle failed to keep a 'safe distance' alone had resulted in the alleged road traffic accident.

(iii) I submit that the Hon'ble Tribunal overlooked the fact that the rider of the motorcycle had no valid driving licence and his lack of driving skill and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/07/2025 07:43:07 pm )
incompetence to maneuver the motor cycle had resulted in the alleged road traffic accident.
(iv) I submit that the first respondent is taking urgent steps, for executing the Final Award.
If he succeeds in his attempt, the Petitioner/Appellant will be forced to pay the erroneous Final Award and all the efforts of the Petitioner/Appellant in preferring the Appeal would turn futile.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submitted that the accident was happened due to the rash and negligent part of the rider of the two-wheeler.
At that time, the rider of the two- wheeler had no license.
Furthermore, the claimant/1st respondent is a pillian rider, and he filed a false claim against the appellant and the 2nd respondent, who are the Insurance Company as well as the owner of the lorry.

4. The learned counsel further pointed out that at the time of athe lleged accident, the lorry belonged to the second respondent, had been repaired and parked on the roadside at that time, the driver of the two- M/S.Tata Aig General vs Raghavan @ Raghavendiran on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29391774/
2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/07/2025 07:43:07 pm ) wheeler hit the lorry due to which, the accident was happened.

entities.text: S.Tata Aig General vs Raghavan @ Raghavendiran
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the Tribunal has erroneously fixed the liability upon the Insurance Company/appellant Hence, he prayed to set aside the findings of the Tribunal.
5.

On perusal of the evidence of PW1 stated that on the date of the alleged accident, the claimant/2nd respondent here in is the pillian amd two two-wheeler was driven by one Balaji, at the time of the accident, the lorry bearing Registration No.TN-51-D-3093 which belongs to the second respondent herein in front of the two-wheeler was stopped suddenly without any indication or signal on the road due to the two- wheeler being dashed against the lorry due to which the claimant/1st respondent herein sustained multiple grievous injuries all over the body.
If, really, the vehicle was stopped on the roadside as alleged by the appellant, they ought to have examined the driver of the lorry to prove the said occurrence.
On perusal of the records, it reveals that the driver of the lorry was not been examined..
Therefore, the appeal grounds https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/07/2025 07:43:07 pm ) raised by the appellant is unsustainable.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the facts and circumstances and award the compensation, which needs no interference.

6. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed and the Judgment and decree dated 05.09.2024 made in M.C.O.P.No.1430 of 2016 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Court II), Small Cases, Chennai is confirmed.
